_about: How well Tip of the Tongue works in each language. English, Spanish, French, Brazilian Portuguese, Hindi and Mandarin were measured on 2026-10-26 with picture sets built from a 20-word list per language (the English demo list, translated). German, Italian, Dutch, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Turkish, Polish, Indonesian and Vietnamese were measured on 2026-10-27 on the English demo set's pictures, named by Muse Spark in each language. Spoken naming was checked with speech synthesized by macOS voices, never recordings of people. Method and caveats: docs/languages.md.

table.recommended_form: the bare word (the article didn't help)
a frame (यह बिल्ली है) was tried and didn't help; use the bare word
with a measure word (一只猫, 一把剪刀)
in a short sentence (Das ist eine Katze)
the bare word (고양이); 예요/이에요 didn't help
in a short sentence (To jest kot)
with the classifier (con mèo, cái ô)

status_levels.verified: Picture set and Muse Spark naming at least 19/20, spoken naming at least 18/20 in the recommended answer form with two voices or runs, and the scoring rules for the language tested. Codes still get a person's review, as in every language.
status_levels.works with review: Pictures and naming work and spoken naming is mostly right in the recommended form (for the languages added Oct 27: at least 16/20 averaged over two runs), but known gaps mean a person should check every code that isn't Correct.
status_levels.experimental: Measured below that, or not measured. Usable for building pictures; don't rely on automatic spoken scoring.

method.picture_sets: scripts/build_test_set.py, line style, 2 candidates per word: Muse Spark plans each picture, Muse Image draws, SAM 3.1 checks for one clear object, Muse Spark names the picture in the test language and naming_errors.classify scores that name. kept = at least one candidate passed both checks. First-pass numbers, before reviewer edits.
method.named_by_muse_spark: Words for which Muse Spark's one-word name for at least one candidate picture was coded Correct.
method.spoken: Each of the 20 words synthesized on its own with macOS `say`, converted to 16 kHz mono WAV, padded with 0.7 s of silence, transcribed by Muse Voice Transcribe with the language hint and coded by naming_errors.classify with the set's accepted alternates, as the Scorer does. correct = transcripts coded Correct. One run of 20 per entry; expect a few points of run-to-run variation.
method.picture_sets_reused: Languages added Oct 27: no new pictures. The translated 20-word list was planned by Muse Spark (accepted spellings, ambiguity flags) and Muse Spark named the English demo set's kept picture in the language; the second picture was named only when the first wasn't coded Correct. SAM 3.1 results come from demo_en (SAM checks the English gloss). kept and named use the final scoring rules; first_pass has the counts at build time.
method.spoken_reruns: Languages added Oct 27: each count is coded with the final rules; correct_at_run is the count when the run was made. Where macOS has one natural voice for a language, both entries are two runs of that voice.
method.live_check: Oct 27: 23 hand-written error responses (2 or 3 per added language: Semantic, Formal, Description) through the real Muse Spark judge; all 23 got the expected code.

untested_languages: Any other language: Test Studio will try (Muse Spark and Muse Image take any language) and Muse Voice Transcribe accepts a hint for 25 languages, of which 16 are measured here. Nothing else is measured, so the status is experimental.

languages.name: English
languages.summary: Reference language: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary and WordNet rules.

recommended.answer_form: the bare word (the article didn't help)

notes: Daniel (en-GB) heard three short or borrowed words as other words: saw -> 'So', harp -> 'huh', igloo -> 'Hey, Blue'.
Samantha wrote 'umbrellaumbrella'. The Scorer now reads a name that was written twice as one word.

languages.name: Spanish
languages.summary: Verified when people name with the article. Bare words depend on the voice: 13/20 with a Spain voice, 18/20 with a Mexican one.
notes: Picture set: Muse Spark called the sierra (saw) pictures 'serrucho' (hand saw); the item went to review.
Bare words from Mónica (es-ES) became spelling variants or near-misses: Kuchara, Cierra, Paraguás, Acla, Baco, Janahoria, Arba.

Counting exact homophones as Correct, as French and Portuguese now do, would make it 15/20 (Mónica) and 20/20 (Paulina). It's not applied, because the brief keeps Spanish scoring unchanged; it's a one-line change (HOMOPHONE_LANGS) for the lead to approve.

languages.name: French
languages.summary: Verified when people name with the article (19/20 and 20/20). Bare one-syllable words are often heard as other words (banc -> 'Dans').
notes: Scoring rules: articles, elision (l'ancre), plurals, rough spelling-to-sound rules, and homophones counted as Correct (une encre -> ancre).
Muse Spark named one of the kettle pictures 'théière' (teapot); the other picture was kept.
Flagged meanings: banc (sandbank, shoal) and bougie (spark plug).
Amélie (fr-CA) got 15/20 on bare words and 20/20 with the article.

languages.name: Brazilian Portuguese
languages.summary: Verified for Brazilian Portuguese when people name with the article (19/20 and 18/20, one Brazilian voice, two runs).
notes: Only one Brazilian macOS voice (Luciana). A European Portuguese voice (Joana) saying the Brazilian words got 14/20 bare and 16/20 with the article.
guarda-chuva is the hardest word: 'Guarda a chuva' and 'Quando ar da chuva'. Hyphenated targets match with or without the hyphen.
Homophone spellings count as Correct (cerrote -> serrote, Senoura -> cenoura).
The plan step stored other spellings (ancora, helicoptero, cactus, igloo) as accepted alternates.
Swapped by a reviewer: the kept cacto picture was green in a line-style set, so the line drawing was used instead.

languages.name: Hindi
languages.summary: Picture sets work; automatic spoken scoring isn't reliable yet (10-14/20).

recommended.answer_form: a frame (यह बिल्ली है) was tried and didn't help; use the bare word

notes: Picture set, two items to review: हार्प (harp) was named वीणा (veena, an Indian instrument). The harp is unfamiliar in India; replace the item.
Picture set: सीटी (whistle) drawings were read as a microphone or an ektara.
Also named: one cactus picture as नागफनी (the native name for prickly pear), and one kettle picture as चायदानी (teapot).
The transcriber sometimes switches script. It wrote loanwords in Latin letters ('cactus', 'Kaitly'; accepted as alternates now) and इग्लू in Bengali (এগুলো).
Fixed: the tokenizer split Hindi words at vowel signs (बिल्ली -> ब ल ल), so no Hindi response could score Correct before Oct 26.
Only one Hindi macOS voice (Lekha); two identical runs gave 13 and 10 (14 and 11 with alternates).

languages.name: Mandarin Chinese
languages.summary: Works when people name with a measure word (18/20 and 17/20). There are no sound-based error codes (Formal, Mixed, Nonword) for Chinese.

recommended.answer_form: with a measure word (一只猫, 一把剪刀)

notes: Bare one-syllable names come back as homophones: 锚 -> 毛 (both máo), 锯子 -> 句子, 竖琴 -> 树禽. Telling them apart needs pinyin, which we don't have offline.
Picture set, two items to review: both 水壶 (kettle) pictures looked like teapots and were named 茶壶; and 手套 was planned as a pair of gloves, so SAM saw two objects.
The plan prompt now asks for exactly one object and no colors. A retry kept a single glove, but 水壶 still drew as a teapot.
Swapped by a reviewer: the kept 胡萝卜 (carrot) picture was orange in a line-style set, so the line drawing was used instead.
Muse Spark named one umbrella picture 伞 instead of 雨伞; it is a good alternate to accept in review.
Fixed: Chinese scoring crashed without the jieba package. It now splits words itself, removes measure words, and maps traditional characters to simplified.

languages.name: German
languages.summary: Verified when people answer in a short sentence, Das ist ein/eine ... (20/20 and 19/20). With der/die/das it was 17/20 twice; bare words 16 and 15.

recommended.answer_form: in a short sentence (Das ist eine Katze)

notes: Anna is the only natural German voice on macOS, so both runs use her.
The kettle picture was named Teekessel. German compounds put the head last, so a compound ending in the name counts (Teekessel for Kessel).
Bare words and der/die/das failed on the same items: Kerze -> Herze/Karte, Harfe -> Hafe, Iglu -> Eglu or nothing. The frame fixed all of them in the first run.

languages.name: Italian
languages.summary: Works with review: 18/20 and 17/20 with the article. bollitore comes back as 'bolitore' (one l) and arpa as 'Art'/'arta'.
notes: Alice is the only natural Italian voice on macOS, so both runs use her.
Both kettle pictures were named teiera (teapot), so bollitore went to review.
Italian elides like French: l'ancora and un'arpa are split before matching; an apostrophe the transcript put inside the name (L'umaca) is ignored.

languages.name: Dutch
languages.summary: Works with review: 16/20 with both voices with een. Long and short vowels get confused: lepel -> label, kaars -> kaas, zaag -> zag.
notes: Xander (Netherlands) and Ellen (Belgium).
The stepladder was named trap (stairs) and trapladder; compounds ending in the name count.
Dutch diminutives (bankje, katje) count as the name.

languages.name: Japanese
languages.summary: Experimental: 16/20 and 15/20 with です, 13 and 15 bare. Kanji homophones (錨 -> 怒り, やかん -> 夜間) are matched by reading, with Muse Spark reading the transcript aloud in hiragana.
notes: Kyoko is the only Japanese voice on macOS, so both runs use her.
The stepladder was named 脚立 (kyatatsu, a stepladder) rather than はしご, so はしご went to review.
Failures the rules can't fix: 猫 -> でこ, パイナップル -> バイナップル, ハープ -> ラープ/ワープ, スプーン -> nothing.

languages.name: Korean
languages.summary: Experimental: bare words 13/20 and 14/20; with the copula 15 and 12. One-syllable names fail most: 닻 -> 탁, 톱 -> nothing.

recommended.answer_form: the bare word (고양이); 예요/이에요 didn't help

notes: Yuna is the only Korean voice on macOS, so both runs use her.
Liaison spellings of the same sounds count (파이네플 for 파인애플, 다치에요 for 닻이에요).
Aspirated and plain stops get confused: 가위 -> 카위, 호루라기 -> 고루라기/코루라기.

languages.name: Arabic
languages.summary: Works with review: 16/20, 17/20 with al-, 14/20 bare twice. Emphatic and plain consonants get confused (صفارة -> السفارة, 'the embassy').
notes: Majed is the only Arabic voice on macOS, so both runs use him.
Both kettle pictures were named إبريق (a jug or teapot), so غلاية went to review.
The transcriber split أناناس into أنا ناس ('I people'); a split name counts when joined.
إغلو came back in Latin letters ('Alhulo', 'Hirou!') or as قالوا.

languages.name: Turkish
languages.summary: Verified when people name with bir (18/20 and 19/20). Bare words 17 and 15: short words came back empty (düdük, iglo, mum).
notes: Yelda is the only Turkish voice on macOS, so both runs use her.
The dotted capital İ (İglo) used to break matching; it is now lowercased to i.
salyangoz comes back as 'Sağ yangoz' or 'sağ yalnız'.

languages.name: Polish
languages.summary: Verified when people answer To jest ... (20/20 and 19/20). Bare words were 14 and 15: kot -> Kup, ławka -> UFK, igloo -> nothing.

recommended.answer_form: in a short sentence (To jest kot)

notes: Zosia is the only Polish voice on macOS, so both runs use her.
Muse Spark named both candle pictures świeca; the list had the diminutive świeczka, so it went to review. Accept świeca in a Polish test.

languages.name: Indonesian
languages.summary: Verified: Ini ... scored 20/20 twice, and bare words 19/20 and 18/20.
notes: Damayanti is the only Indonesian voice on macOS, so both runs use her.
Both kettle pictures were named teko (teapot), so ketel went to review.
iglo comes back as 'iglow'.

languages.name: Vietnamese
languages.summary: Works with review: 15/20 and 18/20 with the classifier, 14 and 15 bare. Tones get lost or changed (cưa -> cơ, xương rồng -> xuống dòng).

recommended.answer_form: with the classifier (con mèo, cái ô)

notes: Linh is the only Vietnamese voice on macOS, so both runs use her.

Asked for 'exactly one word', Muse Spark cut names to one syllable (mỏ neo -> neo) or ran them together (càrốt). Test Studio now asks for every syllable in Vietnamese; the set was rebuilt with that prompt (11/20 named before, 20/20 after).
Marks aren't folded in Vietnamese (mèo 'cat' vs méo 'bent'), but a transcript with no marks at all (thia for thìa) still matches.
